foil.purpose: The cover wordmark, once, in gold. Nothing else is this size.

headline.purpose: One per folio: the Spanish section title, English beneath at 13px.

data.purpose: Every value, code and date. Martian Mono caps at 82% width.

mrz.purpose: Forty-four characters per line, sized from its container by cqw, floored at 11px.

legend.purpose: The ICAO dual label: Spanish over English, weight-separated, both always printed.

note.purpose: The tool's own voice. Archivo, never Literata.

prose.purpose: The holder speaking, verbatim, and nowhere else on the surface. 68ch measure.

action.purpose: Every button label on both planes. Micro-caps at 0.1em.

stamp.purpose: The impression's title, over a mono date.

widget-lead.purpose: The quoted value. The largest text in the panel is always something you wrote.

widget-label.purpose: Provenance, destination, measurement. Monospace is data, not costume.

shadows.name: laminate-thickness
shadows.purpose: A laminated card's own thickness: bright top edge, hairline border, contact shadow, one deep cast in the cover's colour.

shadows.name: cover-object
shadows.purpose: The closed booklet as an object on a desk.

shadows.name: page-block
shadows.purpose: The stack of pages along the cover's right edge, so the booklet has a thickness you can count.

shadows.name: field-focus
shadows.purpose: Doubles the field's baseline rule on focus. The only place iris appears as a line rather than as print.

shadows.name: prose-focus
shadows.purpose: The prose field's focus, inset so the box does not grow.

shadows.name: widget-pill
shadows.purpose: Enough lift to read as an object, small enough to be ignorable. Tinted, never black.

shadows.name: widget-panel
shadows.purpose: The open panel's deeper cast. Always paired with a 1px slate-700/80 ring so separation survives a dark host page.

motion.name: turn
motion.purpose: The cover turning: perspective(1800px) rotateY(-96deg) about the left edge. The one large authored motion.

motion.name: page-in
motion.purpose: A folio arriving: 2.6deg about the left edge plus a 6px slide. The short version of the cover's turn, so the surface has one motion idea.

motion.name: print
motion.purpose: Ink drying into the laminate: opacity, a 2px rise, a 1.4% scale and a 1.4px blur resolving.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: The stamp landing: 1.5x collapsing to 1 at its own seeded angle. Never elastic - ink meeting paper decelerates hard.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: The guilloche's stroke-dashoffset resolving. Used once, by the issuance sequence.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every border, background and colour transition on a control or a field.

motion.name: issuance-timeline
motion.value: print 90ms, legends 1050ms, values 1560ms, zone 3260ms, note 4620ms, stamped 5460ms
motion.purpose: The issuance sequence, cumulative. Tuned against the real thing being watched, not to a grid.

narrative.northStar: The Document You Issue To Yourself
narrative.overview:
This system governs two surfaces, and it is honest about the fact that only one of them has been built in the new world. The document is the options page and the browser-action popup: a machine-readable personal document with a burgundy-black cover, one cold laminate plane holding the user's own words, iris-print guilloche seeded from their own name, and gold foil on the cover. Its thesis refuses the onboarding wizard's progress bar: completeness is the MRZ's own '<' filler, and every field states its condition of access rather than wearing a grey pill. The story is the whole reason the form fits: nobody issues this to you. The issuing authority in the machine-readable zone is the literal string OWN, there is no country and no nationality anywhere, and the closing sequence is called Expedicion - the issuance. You type, and the document becomes valid.

The in-page widget is the panel that appears over third-party forms. It is unchanged by this work, still shipping, and its own system is preserved. Its north star is 'Your File, Projected': dark slate chrome, a source-first ledger, four state colours, and your own words on the one light surface. It has not been migrated to the document's palette. That is a real gap, not a pending refinement.

The two surfaces are not arbitrary neighbours. Six rules were inherited on purpose: the One Light Surface Rule, the Content-Before-Hue Rule, the Measured Fold Rule, the Drawn Icon Rule, the Tinted Shadow Rule, and the Pixel Ramp Rule. The clearest of them is the first: on both surfaces, light means the user's own words, and the code says so in both places. Density is a printed document's, not an app's: micro-caps legends at 8.5px, values at 14px in a narrow mono, one heading per folio, and no card inside a card. Nothing is decorative except the guilloche, and the guilloche says so in its own markup - aria-hidden, because a guilloche carries no information.
keyCharacteristics: One cold laminate plane on a burgundy-black ground; light is always the holder's.
Three faces with three jobs: Archivo says the tool is talking, Martian Mono says a machine reads this, Literata says a person wrote it - and Literata appears nowhere else.
Completeness is reported by the MRZ's own '<' filler. No bar, no ring, no percentage, anywhere on either surface.
Every field states its condition of access as a printed endorsement, never a grey pill.
Two inks, two meanings, and never swapped: vermilion is a limitation on the document; archival violet is a condition of access.
Ruled hairlines instead of boxes; borders earn their place one at a time.
Everything derived from the holder's own data is seeded, not random: the same name yields the same rosette, document number and stamp angle, forever.

rules.name: The One Light Surface Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one light plane per surface and it belongs to the holder. On the document that is the laminate; on the widget it is slate-50. Nothing structural, nothing chrome, and nothing belonging to the tool is ever laminate-coloured. The light IS the signal for 'this is yours'. Inherited on purpose from the widget, and the stylesheet says so.

rules.name: The Two Inks, Two Meanings Rule
rules.body: Vermilion (endorse-600) means exactly one thing: a limitation on the document - the INCOMPLETO endorsement, a refused credential, an over-length answer. Archival violet (stamp-violet) carries a condition of access: a permanent, neutral fact, and specifically not a warning. They were one ink at first, and the collision was a real defect: 'this value never leaves your machine' is the reassuring fact on the page, and it was the only thing coloured like an error.

rules.name: The Content-Before-Hue Rule
rules.body: Two states in the same family are never distinguished by hue alone. The widget's record is the origin: measured against each other their fills were the same colour and their text 18 degrees apart in the same family, so a colour-only distinction was never going to carry it. The fix was to give the caution something the banner structurally cannot have - the value already in the field, quoted. Hue reinforces the split; it never carries it.

rules.name: The Border-Only Ink Rule
rules.body: intaglio-400 measures 3.63:1 on the laminate: it clears the 3:1 non-text floor and fails the 4.5:1 text floor, so it is permitted on borders and forbidden on text. The boundary exists because the English half of every bilingual label was set in it - the second line of every field on the surface was its least legible text, on a product whose stated commitment is that it works in both languages.

rules.name: The Cold Laminate Rule
rules.body: The light plane is #eef1ea and its family: cold, with a green cast. Not cream, not ivory, not warm white. Named in the code as the single most likely way to lose this world.

rules.name: The Foil Never Touches The Laminate Rule
rules.body: Gold is the cover's material, and it never appears on the light plane. The build's three uses outside the closed cover are all on burgundy: the rail's current-page marker, the issuance entry, and the header wordmark. Gold-on-burgundy everywhere would be the cliche this world is one bad decision away from.

rules.name: The Face Names The Author Rule
rules.body: You can tell who wrote a string from the face it is set in. Martian Mono means a machine reads it; Literata means a person wrote it; Archivo means the tool is talking. The first build set the tool's own notes in Literata too, which quietly broke the one typographic rule the surface has: if the reading face also carries the tool talking, it marks nothing.

rules.name: The Printed Bilingual Label Rule
rules.body: Every field label prints Spanish over English, always, in the same ink, separated by weight. The interview has stored every label as an {en, es} pair since long before the redesign, and a data page prints both by construction - which is why the language toggle that used to swap labels is gone. It now sets only which language the holder's own prose is written in.

rules.name: The Pixel Ramp Rule
rules.body: Type sizes are absolute pixels on both surfaces, never the rem-based scale. On the widget the reason is environmental: the shadow root isolates the cascade but not the root font size, and a panel that shrinks to 9px on a host page with html { font-size: 12px } is illegible through no fault of its own. On the document it keeps micro-caps legends at the one size they were measured at.

rules.name: The Case Is Not Cosmetic Rule
rules.body: Caps are a display transform and never touch the stored value - but where case carries meaning, the transform is switched off by name. The repository line lost the capitals of the filename the whole product is named after; an email shown back as MARTIN@TAXDOWN.ES when it was typed in lower case makes the user doubt what actually reached the file, and the one thing this surface cannot afford is doubt about what it stored.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No micro-caps line is stacked directly above a heading. The folio number sits in the page's top corner where a bound document prints its page number, because a micro-caps line directly over a heading is an eyebrow whatever it contains, and the heading carries itself.

rules.name: The Measured Fold Rule
rules.body: An edge fade is applied only when the content actually overflows, measured and re-measured on scroll and resize, never applied unconditionally. On the document: a forty-four character line clipped flat at the edge of the page does not read as 'there is more'; it reads as a wrong check digit, on the one element of the surface whose whole claim is that its digits are right. Inherited from the widget's ledger, where an edge fade on content that fits is a lie about the content.

rules.name: The Legible Line Rule
rules.body: Forty-four characters must fit on one line at every width, sized by container query rather than breakpoint - but with an 11px floor. On a 375px viewport, fitting forty-four characters put the line at 8px, and a machine-readable zone nobody can read is a worse outcome than one you swipe, which is also how you read the real thing.

rules.name: The Thumb Edge Rule
rules.body: Navigation and progress are the same object. A closed passport shows the stack of its pages and which are stamped before you open any of them, so the rail carries a mark per folio and an MRZ '<' where a page is still empty - one vocabulary for 'nothing here yet'. It replaced two counters that said the same thing while looking like homework.

rules.name: The Narrow Rail Rule
rules.body: Below the two-column breakpoint the vertical rail was 719px tall on a 375px viewport - fourteen entries to scroll past before reaching a single field, which is the whole surface's first impression spent on a table of contents. It becomes what a closed booklet actually shows edge-on: one scroll-snapped row of folio numbers.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is cast in the colour of the ground it falls on, never in black. The page's cast is the cover's own burgundy, because a black shadow under a card on burgundy reads as a sticker dropped on it. The widget's is its own slate, for the same stated reason on a white ATS form. Same rule, two grounds.

rules.name: The Flat Interior Rule
rules.body: Nothing inside a laminate page casts a shadow, and nothing inside the widget panel does either. Separation is a hairline rule or a tonal fill. The one inset shadow on the surface is the focus state's, and it is 1px.

rules.name: The Material Not Modal Rule
rules.body: Depth says 'this is an object made of layers', never 'this floats above the app'. Blind embossing carries no ink at all - only the highlight and shadow a die leaves - and the foil wordmark is a gradient because the material on the object being drawn is literally a metal foil. Gradient lettering is a habit this world earns; it is not licence for gradients elsewhere.

rules.name: The Drawn Icon Rule
rules.body: Every mark on either surface is drawn geometry - inline SVG or CSS borders - inheriting currentColor. No emoji, no icon font, no img. The widget's reason is environmental: a host font can substitute a glyph, and a tool whose padlock renders as a tofu box on someone else's page has lost the argument it was making. The document's is material: a document's marks are struck, not typed.

rules.name: The Own Control Rule
rules.body: No stock operating-system control survives inside the document. The native checkbox was a rounded blue-grey system square in the middle of a page whose every other border is a hairline rule. The textarea's resize grabber was the one piece of operating-system furniture visible anywhere inside the document, sitting in the corner of the field that holds the most personal thing on the page.

rules.name: The Seeded Not Random Rule
rules.body: Anything generated from the holder's data is derived from it deterministically, so the same input yields the same mark forever: the rosette's geometry from the name, the stamp's angle and ink from the record's key, the document number from the transliterated name. A random one would look identical and mean nothing, and a stamp that jittered to a new angle on every render would be decoration pretending to be evidence.

rules.name: The One Spine Rule
rules.body: Everything that arrives on the document arrives by turning about the left edge, because that is where the binding is. There is no fade-up, no slide-in from the right, and no scale-from-centre anywhere on the surface. The folio's 2.6-degree turn is the short version of the cover's 96-degree one, so the surface has one motion idea rather than two unrelated ones.

rules.name: The Finished State Rule
rules.body: Every keyframe runs with 'both' and ends on the resting value, so prefers-reduced-motion cancels the animation and keeps the finished document. Reduced motion yields a complete page, never an invisible one.

rules.name: The Nothing Truncates Rule
rules.body: Inside a widget row text wraps; it does not truncate. At 390px a truncating destination clipped the very thing the user has to read before committing. The one surviving truncate is the header's domain subtitle, which is chrome, not a commitment.

dos: Do keep exactly one light plane per surface, and keep it for the holder's own words. Laminate on the document, slate-50 in the widget.
Do state a condition of access as a printed endorsement - a dashed rule and a violet legend - not as a pill, a badge or a grey chip.
Do use vermilion only for a limitation on the document, and archival violet only for a condition of access. Never swap them; never render a reassurance in the alarm ink.
Do report completeness with the MRZ's own '<' filler and the rail's marks. A '<' is the system's word for 'nothing here yet', on both the line and the rail.
Do print both languages on every field label, in the same ink, separated by weight.
Do set values and codes in Martian Mono caps, the tool's own voice in Archivo, and the holder's prose in Literata - and switch caps off by name (--exact, --verbatim) wherever case carries meaning.
Do declare type sizes in absolute pixels on both surfaces.
Do cast every shadow in the colour of the ground it falls on.
Do measure before applying an edge fade, and re-measure on scroll and resize.
Do put minmax(0,1fr) on every grid track that can contain the MRZ, single-column layouts included.
Do seed anything generated from the holder's data, so the same name yields the same rosette, number and stamp angle forever.
Do draw every mark - inline SVG or CSS borders - inheriting currentColor.
Do keep every font file bundled and subset to latin + latin-ext.
Do let a disabled control stay readable enough to say what it will do once it is available (intaglio-700 on laminate-200, 7.78:1).
donts: Don't put intaglio-400 on text. It is 3.63:1 - a border ink only.
Don't warm the laminate toward cream. It is #eef1ea, cold, green-cast.
Don't put foil on the laminate. Gold belongs to the burgundy.
Don't add a progress bar, a ring, a percentage or an 'N of M' counter to either surface. The filler and the rail already report it.
Don't distinguish two states in the same colour family by hue alone. Give one of them different content.
Don't leave a stock operating-system control inside the document - no native checkbox square, no resize grabber.
Don't let the MRZ wrap, and don't let it shrink below 11px to avoid scrolling.
Don't stack a micro-caps line directly above a heading. That is an eyebrow whatever it contains.
Don't re-roll a seeded value on render. A stamp that moves is an animation, not a record.
Don't overshoot on the stamp press, or spring any motion on this surface. Ink meeting paper decelerates hard.
Don't add a country, a nationality, an ISO 3166 code, or a crest anywhere.
Don't invent a photograph, a date, or a clause the file does not hold.
Don't put a status colour on text smaller than 11px (the widget's earlier 10px caution was a defect).
Don't add a second light surface, an emoji, an icon font, an X-to-close, or a sparkle on either surface.
Don't apply a decorative overlay unconditionally.
